cues.zh: 自从我上传了几段这台8位可编程计算机的视频后，
cues.en: Ever since I uploaded a few videos of this 8-bit programmable computer,

cues.zh: 这是我之前搭建的，我收到了很多关于它的问题。
cues.en: that I built a while ago, I've gotten a lot of questions about it.

cues.zh: 我想回答几个最常见的问题，
cues.en: I wanted to answer a few of the most common questions,

cues.zh: 而到目前为止最最常见的问题，
cues.en: and definitely by far the most common question,

cues.zh: 就是：“你能教我们怎么搭建它吗？”或者“你有它的电路图吗？”
cues.en: is, "can you show us how to build it?" or "do you have schematics for this?"

cues.zh: 或者类似这样的问题。答案是，信不信由你，我其实没有这台东西的电路图，
cues.en: Or something along those lines. The answer is, believe it or not, I actually don't have schematics

cues.zh: 我从来没有坐下来画过完整的电路图。
cues.en: for this thing, I never sat down and drew out a full schematic.

cues.zh: 因为一切都很模块化，或者说这个架构非常模块化，
cues.en: Because of how modular everything is, or how modular this architecture is,

cues.zh: 我能够单独搭建每一个部分，搭建、测试、实验，
cues.en: I was able to build each piece of it by itself, and build it, and test it, and experiment with

cues.zh: 一次一个模块，然后再把它们组装起来。直到所有部件组合在一起，
cues.en: one module at a time, before I had to put it all together. It wasn't really until all the pieces came together

cues.zh: 我才真正需要更仔细地思考它们整体如何运作。
cues.en: that I really had to be a little bit more thoughtful about how it was all going to work.

cues.zh: 为此我在这本书里找到了一个很好的参考模型，我强烈推荐，
cues.en: For that I had this really good model to follow in this book that I really recommend,

cues.zh: 《数字计算机电子学》，作者 Albert Paul Malvino。
cues.en: "Digital Computer Electronics", by Albert Paul Malvino.

cues.zh: 可惜这本书应该已经绝版了，但希望你能在网上找到二手书
cues.en: Unfortunately, I think the book is out of print, but hopefully you can find a used copy online

cues.zh: 之类的。这本书里有种架构……有好几种架构。
cues.en: or something. This book has an architecture... has a couple architectures.

cues.zh: 其中一种是 SAP-1，也就是“尽可能简单”。目标是做一个非常简单的计算机架构，
cues.en: One is the SAP-1, which is, "simple as possible". The goal is to be a very simple computer architecture,

cues.zh: 展示计算机运行背后的所有关键概念，
cues.en: that demonstrates all the crucial ideas behind computer operation

cues.zh: 同时又不会不必要地复杂。
cues.en: without being any more complicated than it needs to be.

cues.zh: 书里的这个架构，基本上就是我遵循的模型，
cues.en: The architecture that they have in here, is basically the model that I followed,

cues.zh: 是我搭建这台计算机的基础。你可以看到所有相同的组件都在那里。
cues.en: what I based this computer on. So you can see that all of the same components are there.

cues.zh: 这里有程序计数器，还有内存地址寄存器，
cues.en: There's a program counter here, there's the memory address register,

cues.zh: 用到的16字节内存，可编程只读存储器，
cues.en: the 16 bytes of memory that are used, programmable read only memory,

cues.zh: 我有RAM，但就操作而言，两者没什么区别。
cues.en: I've got RAM but, same difference, as far as the operation is concerned.

cues.zh: 指令寄存器、控制单元，就是下面这一堆东西，
cues.en: An instruction register, the control unit, which is all this stuff down here,

cues.zh: 你可以看到它们发出所有这些信号，又回传到
cues.en: and you can see that they have all these signals going out, that come back in

cues.zh: 其他所有组件，这些黄线就是干这个的。
cues.en: to all the other components, and that's what all these yellow wires are.

cues.zh: 它们都是控制信号。从控制单元发出，
cues.en: They're all the control signals. They come from the control unit and go out

cues.zh: 传到各个不同部件，协调一切运作。
cues.en: to all the different pieces to orchestrate everything.

cues.zh: 累加器，就是这里的A寄存器。ALU，即算术
cues.en: The accumulator, which is the A register here. The ALU, which is the arithmetic

cues.zh: 逻辑单元，在这台计算机里只做加减法。
cues.en: logic unit, which in this computer, just adds and subtracts.

cues.zh: 这些是它唯一会做的算术运算。
cues.en: Those are the only arithmetic operations it knows how to do.

cues.zh: 然后是 B 寄存器。A 和 B 寄存器是算术运算的输入。
cues.en: And then the B register. The A and the B register are the inputs for the arithmetic.

cues.zh: 输出寄存器有二进制显示，我做了个十进制显示
cues.en: And the output register, they have a binary display, I've got a decimal display

cues.zh: 我觉得这样更好看一点。
cues.en: which I thought was a little nicer.

cues.zh: 这是我做的一个改进。
cues.en: That's one enhancement that I made.

cues.zh: 我还做了几处其他改进，主要是围绕指令集
cues.en: I made a few other enhancements to this as well, primarily around the instruction set

cues.zh: 以及你实际能用它做什么。
cues.en: and what you can actually do with it.

cues.zh: 书里的这个模型讲的是指令包含
cues.en: The model here in the book, it talks about the instructions having a

cues.zh: “加载 A”指令、加法指令、减法、输出和停机，就这些。
cues.en: "load A" instruction, an add instruction, subtract, output, and halt, and that's it.

cues.zh: 我加了几个别的。我加了一个立即数加载，让你能
cues.en: I added a couple other things. I added a load immediate, which just lets you

cues.zh: 省一点内存，如果你想往 A 寄存器里加载某个特定值的话。
cues.en: save a little bit of memory, if you wanted to load a particular value into the A register.

cues.zh: 然后是一条“store A”指令，除了“load A”从内存加载累加器之外
cues.en: And then a "store A" command, which in addition to the "load A," which loads the accumulator

cues.zh: 你还可以把累加器里的内容存回内存。
cues.en: from memory, you can store what's in the accumulator to memory.

cues.zh: 这样就能编写稍微复杂一点的程序了。
cues.en: So that let's you build a little bit more complex programs.

cues.zh: 我还加入了跳转指令，我觉得这对可编程计算机来说相当重要
cues.en: I also added jump instructions, which I thought were pretty important

cues.zh: 有一条常规跳转指令，
cues.en: for a programmable computer. There's a regular jump instruction,

cues.zh: 还有一条条件跳转指令，当进位位被置位时就会跳转，
cues.en: there's also a conditional jump instruction, that jumps when the carry bit is set,

cues.zh: 也就是加法溢出的时候。
cues.en: anytime the addition over flows.

cues.zh: 所以你可能还在想，能不能直接告诉我怎么造这个东西，
cues.en: So you might still be wondering, can I just tell you how to build this thing already,

cues.zh: 你能不能画个原理图之类的？好消息是，
cues.en: can you draw up a schematic or something like that? Well, I've got some good news.

cues.zh: 这正是我打算做的，做一系列视频，把整个过程的每一步都讲一遍。
cues.en: That is exactly what I plan to do, to make a bunch of videos, that go through every step of the process.

cues.zh: 我打算从零开始，完整复刻一台这样的计算机，
cues.en: I am planning to actually build a whole new copy of this computer from scratch,

cues.zh: 并把全过程都录成视频。坏消息是，这得花不少时间。
cues.en: and have videos of all of it. The bad news is that it's going to take a while.

cues.zh: 可惜我空闲时间不多，但我给自己定的目标是每周至少做一期视频，
cues.en: I don't have a ton of free time, unfortunately, but my personal goal is to make one video a week,

cues.zh: 至少一期吧。那就看看进展如何，但即便如此，我也要确保
cues.en: at a minimum. So we'll see how well that goes, but even with that, I want to make sure I'm covering

cues.zh: 一切都从基本原理讲起，不留下任何未解之谜，把每个环节为什么这样运作都讲清楚。
cues.en: everything from first principles, not leaving any mystery about why things work the way that they do.

cues.zh: 我不想让你们凭空相信任何东西，但一步步来的话，
cues.en: I don't wanna ask you to take anything on faith, but going step by step,

cues.zh: 可能得花挺久才能讲到所有内容。所以至少……
cues.en: probably means it's going to take a while to get to everything. So at least...

cues.zh: 至少几个月吧，可能更久。我希望这份等待是值得的。我的目标是，而且我坚信
cues.en: at least a few months. Probably longer. I hope that it will be worth the wait. My goal, and I'm convinced that

cues.zh: 任何人都能造出这台计算机。只要你有足够的耐心，仔细地把线都接好，
cues.en: anyone can build this computer. As long as you're patient enough to wire it all up, carefully,

cues.zh: 并且有毅力去排查那些不可避免的接错线、
cues.en: and you have the persistence to troubleshoot the inevitable wrong connections,

cues.zh: 断线之类的问题。我坚信任何人都能造出它，并真正深入理解
cues.en: or broken connections or something. I'm convinced that anyone can build this and really understand

cues.zh: 计算机的工作原理，通过亲手搭建来理解。即使你完全没有
cues.en: at a very deep level, how a computer works, by building this. Even if you, don't have any experience with

cues.zh: 这方面的经验，或者没有电子学基础。事实上我特别希望、特别期待看到这一幕，
cues.en: this sort of thing, or with electronics. In fact I really hope, I'm really looking forward to that happening, and

cues.zh: 看到大家动手做这些东西，甚至把它改进得更好。所以，我想接下来的几期视频，我会
cues.en: people building these things, and improving on it even. So, I think for the next videos, I'm going to be

cues.zh: 接下来一周我要出差，所以下一个视频可能要等两三周才能上线。
cues.en: traveling over the next week, so it may be in a couple weeks before I can get the next video up.

cues.zh: 我的目标是先聚焦时钟，把它作为第一步，然后一步步带大家
cues.en: My goal is to just start focusing on the clock, as the first steps, and walk through

cues.zh: 从零开始搭建这个时钟电路。这里有几个有意思的地方。
cues.en: building this, the clock circuit, from scratch. There's a couple interesting things going on here.

cues.zh: 时钟当然负责协调计算机里的一切，所有东西的时序。
cues.en: The clock, of course, coordinates everything in the computer, the timing of everything.

cues.zh: 这里你可以调节时钟的速度，可以看到我把它调慢了，
cues.en: In this case, you can adjust the speed of the clock, you can see here I'm slowing it down,

cues.zh: 于是其他所有东西都运行得更慢。你也可以停掉时钟，然后一步一步单步执行，
cues.en: so everything else is running slower. You can also stop the clock, and then step one step at a time,

cues.zh: 这在排查问题时非常有用——如果某处不工作，而这几乎不可避免，
cues.en: which is very useful for troubleshooting something, if something isn't working, which inevitably,

cues.zh: 你搭这个的时候总会遇到某处不工作的情况，那时你就需要
cues.en: if you build this you're going to run into a point where something isn't working, and you need to

cues.zh: 一步步来。时钟有几个特点，它用的是555定时器，
cues.en: go step by step. A couple features that are of the clock, is that it uses the 5-5-5 timers,

cues.zh: 所以我会讲讲它们是怎么工作的，以及它们在时钟电路里
cues.en: so I will go through how those work, and they're being used in a couple different applications,

cues.zh: 的几个不同应用。所以，我想这就是我接下来要做的事，下一系列视频。
cues.en: in the clock circuit. So, I think that that's the next thing that I'll do, the next set of videos.

cues.zh: 你可以期待看到这些内容。希望你们和我一样兴奋。
cues.en: You can look forward to seeing those. I hope you're as excited as I am about this.

cues.zh: 再次请大家耐心一些，全部讲完需要一段时间，
cues.en: Again, I ask for your patience, it's going to take a while to get through it all,

cues.zh: 但我希望这是值得的。如果这让你感到兴奋，请给这个视频点个赞，
cues.en: but I hope it will be worth it. If this is exciting to you, please give this video a thumbs up,

cues.zh: 并订阅频道，告诉你的朋友们，因为如果你喜欢看到的内容，
cues.en: and subscribe to the channel, tell all your friends, cause if you like what you see,

cues.zh: 知道人们觉得这些视频有价值，对我来说真的很受鼓舞，所以
cues.en: knowing that people find these videos valuable, is really motivating to me, so

cues.zh: 订阅并观看视频，老实说，是确保我
cues.en: subscribing and watching the videos, is honestly the best way to make sure that I

cues.zh: 继续做下去的最好方式。感谢观看。
cues.en: keep working on them. Thanks for watching.
